Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary: Acute onset (≈30 minutes post ingestion) of progressive upper lip angioedema after prawn soup with dyspnea, throat tightness, and dizziness in a patient with asthma and known peanut allergy. Prior similar episode after restaurant food. No medications taken prior to call.  
- Relevant DDx (consistent with transcript):  
  - Anaphylaxis due to IgE-mediated shellfish (prawn) allergy—most likely given rapid time course, airway symptoms, dizziness, and atopic history.  
  - IgE-mediated acute allergic angioedema to shellfish without full anaphylaxis—possible but less likely due to systemic respiratory symptoms.  
  - Contact urticaria/oral allergy syndrome—less likely; does not explain systemic symptoms.  
- Working diagnosis: Anaphylaxis secondary to probable new shellfish (prawn) allergy.  
- Management during encounter: Immediate emergency response initiated—advised to call ambulance; take available antihistamine while awaiting EMS; ensure supervision by mother.  
- Post-acute considerations (to be completed after hospital discharge):  
  - Prescribe epinephrine auto-injectors and provide an anaphylaxis action plan.  
  - Referral to Allergy/Immunology for evaluation (skin testing/specific IgE) to shellfish and review of peanut allergy.  
  - Asthma control review and inhaler technique check; consider need for controller therapy if indicated (not assessed today).  
  - Allergen avoidance counseling (shellfish and cross-contamination precautions).  
- Conflict noted: None between transcript and DDx.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Anaphylaxis due to IgE-mediated shellfish (prawn) allergy — High likelihood: Rapid-onset angioedema with dyspnea and dizziness within 30–60 minutes of prawn ingestion in an atopic patient.  
- IgE-mediated acute allergic angioedema to shellfish without full anaphylaxis — Medium likelihood: Localized lip swelling after shellfish exposure, but systemic symptoms make anaphylaxis more likely.  
- Contact urticaria/oral allergy syndrome — Low-Medium likelihood: Initial localized lip symptoms after direct contact; systemic respiratory symptoms argue against this as sole diagnosis.
